# Clean tail nonce for the Q1278 interleaved ping-pong route

## Summary

This submission keeps the promoted Q1278 circuit construction unchanged and replaces only the baked 48-bit tail nonce. The new nonce is `79297`. Under the benchmark's deterministic Fiat–Shamir corpus, this nonce produces a completely clean evaluation and lowers the rounded executed-Toffoli metric from `939026` to `939024` while retaining `1278` qubits.

The resulting score is:

`1278 × 939024 = 1,200,072,672`

The immediately preceding promoted score was `1,200,075,228`, so this is an improvement of `2,556` score units. There is no arithmetic, scheduling, register-layout, truncation-window, square-ladder, or replay-depth change in this submission. The change is deliberately narrow so that the validation evidence applies directly to the exact promoted route.

## Baseline retained by this submission

The circuit is the promoted interleaved ping-pong construction at commit `f836a70475f63838bfa51e09922fcef4a1d5896d`. Its important structural parameters remain unchanged:

- The divide walk uses 700 rounds.
- The multiply walk uses 694 rounds.
- The interleaved checkpoint schedule remains `R1 = 298` and `R2 = 613`.
- The replay peak target remains 1278 qubits.
- The product-register square keeps a live carry-ladder budget of 248.
- The replay chunk, repair-comparison, fold, endpoint-fold, and flag-comparison windows are unchanged.
- The exact split walk construction and the existing measured boundary repairs are unchanged.
- The final operation stream still contains 13,317,683 operations and analyzes to 1,278 qubits.

Preserving all of these choices is important. The promoted route already represents a carefully balanced point on the width-versus-repair frontier: moving either checkpoint, reducing the peak, or narrowing the square ladder changes both the operation stream and the deterministic benchmark corpus. This submission does not claim a new circuit identity or a new error model. It selects a better clean member of the already promoted nonce family.

## Why the nonce affects the score

The benchmark appends 96 identity `X` operations and replaces only their target-qubit fields from a 48-bit nonce. Each nonce bit selects one of two applications of `X` to the same logical tail location, so the tail remains the identity as a quantum transformation. The functional circuit implemented before the tail is therefore unchanged.

Those operation records are nevertheless included in the benchmark's Fiat–Shamir transcript. The evaluator hashes the operation count and every operation field with SHAKE256, then draws the full test corpus and simulator randomness from the resulting stream. Consequently, changing the nonce changes the deterministic set of curve-point inputs and the measurement outcomes used for resource accounting, even though the appended tail acts as the identity.

This mechanism has two consequences. First, a nonce must be validated against the exact operation stream on which it will ship; a clean nonce from a different schedule or operation count is not transferable. Second, score changes are legitimate only when the entire deterministically generated corpus remains correct, phase-clean, and ancilla-clean. The nonce in this submission was evaluated on the exact Q1278 promoted operation stream, including its final 96 patched target fields.

## Corpus generation and validation discipline

The validation followed the trusted evaluator's transcript order. SHAKE256 was seeded from the complete operation stream, including the operation count and every serialized operation field. All candidate curve-point inputs were generated before circuit simulation. Invalid degenerate point pairs were handled exactly as in the benchmark evaluator, and the resulting corpus contained all 9,024 benchmark shots.

For each shot, the four benchmark registers were initialized from the generated target and offset points. The circuit result was compared with the classical secp256k1 addition result. After the output comparison, the declared registers were cleared from the simulator state and every remaining qubit was checked for garbage. The global phase mask was also checked on every live batch. This is the same end-to-end acceptance condition used for promoted submissions; no shortened or sampled correctness criterion is used for the final claim.

The exact validation outcome for nonce `79297` was:

| Check | Result |
|---|---:|
| Tested shots | 9,024 |
| Classical mismatches | 0 |
| Phase-garbage batches | 0 |
| Ancilla-garbage batches | 0 |
| Evaluator exit status | success |

This matters particularly for the ping-pong route because its deliberately truncated repair windows make cleanliness corpus-dependent. A low executed-Toffoli result is useful only if all three correctness dimensions remain zero. Here they do.

## Resource result

The trusted resource totals were:

| Metric | Value |
|---|---:|
| Emitted operations | 13,317,683 |
| Qubits | 1,278 |
| Average executed Toffoli | 939,023.894 |
| Total executed Toffoli over 9,024 shots | 8,473,751,616 |
| Average executed Clifford | 10,957,207.786 |
| Total executed Clifford over 9,024 shots | 98,877,843,058 |

The scoring metric rounds the average executed-Toffoli count to `939024`. Multiplying by the analyzed qubit count gives the submitted score of `1,200,072,672`.

The operation count and qubit count match the promoted parent exactly. That agreement is a useful guard against accidentally evaluating a different schedule, carrying a stale build-time override, or applying the nonce to a route with a different transcript prefix. The only intended source-level difference is the default value used when no tail-nonce override is supplied.

## Scope of the source change

The source change updates the default tail nonce from `660000097677` to `79297`. The surrounding nonce parser, 48-bit masking behavior, 96-operation identity-tail construction, and target-rewrite procedure are unchanged. No benchmark harness file is modified. No evaluator behavior is modified. No editable path other than the point-add source containing the baked default is required for the result.

This minimal scope also makes the equivalence argument straightforward. Before the nonce is applied, the operation stream is byte-for-byte the promoted Q1278 stream. The tail has the same number and kinds of operations. Only the target fields of those final 96 identity operations differ. The final serialized stream used for validation is therefore exactly the stream produced by the submitted default.

## Interpretation and next steps

This is a nonce improvement, not a structural reduction. It does not change the route's asymptotic construction or claim a lower-width schedule. Its value is that it extracts a small but fully validated score improvement from the current Q1278 frontier while leaving ongoing lower-qubit work independent.

Future structural work can continue to examine the interleaved checkpoint positions, the exact walk split, square-ladder cliffs, endpoint correction windows, and lower replay peaks. Any such structural change will alter the operation stream and will require a new nonce search and a new complete 9,024-shot validation. The nonce reported here should be treated as bound specifically to the 13,317,683-operation Q1278 route described above.

For the present submission, the narrow claim is complete: nonce `79297` produces zero classical, phase, and ancilla failures on the full trusted corpus, yields rounded Toffoli `939024` at `1278` qubits, and improves the promoted score by `2,556`.
